title: Leaving for London to arrange for Henry Hall and the BBC
summary: Leonard Feather's letter brought him to London to arrange for the BBC dance orchestra under union limits on playing.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Right. Now what was the occasion then, when you left Paris for London? How did that come about?
Well, I received a letter from Leonard Feather, and wanting to know if I would be interested in coming to London to arrange for the BBC dance orchestra,
which was led by Henry Hall. And I answered to Leonard that I would be interested, and the next thing you know, I was on my way to London, and the next thing you know, I was in London.
Yeah. Then you simply left the Willie Lewis orchestra.
You gave them notice and went to London. You were waiting then to see what the next European or British experience would then bring.
Did you know before you went to London that you would not be allowed to play regularly, according to the union rules?
Yes, I knew that, but you know, we had the feeling that maybe after some respectable period of time, that might be relaxed a little, you know.
But it never was relaxed, though.
It never was during the time I was there with -- only one occasion when they allowed me to do one concert at the Hippodrome, you know, and at this concert, I used all British musicians.
Right. That was, I think, in '37?
And it was -- that's the one
And that's the one that was sponsored, I believe, by the Melody Makers, right?
